title: Retain the visible native destination on a pointer takeover from wheel scrubbing

scope.subject: Hand over a positive native Galaxy scrub passage to existing fixed-point orbit on the first real mouse or touch drag, with no position or viewing-direction discontinuity.

research_summary: Exact production Pages and candidate 8a755e61 both lose the native fixed pivot when three trusted inward wheel samples move to ~0.749 and a real drag interrupts before .750. Both leave CameraController free, freeze camera position and move projected real HELION from x720 to x420.589. In pinned YEIS CameraController goToPoint clears anchor/mode; natural completion promotes destination point to native orbit but product scrub never reaches time-based completion and existing drag cancels before controller update. Reuse exact current gotoPoint anchor and revision; restore prior quaternion after installing fixed orbit; leave real free, non-drag inputs and zero-position return alone.

sources.finding: Current pinned native renderer remains the authority; no upstream patch or new camera.
The current R3F scene uses a shared React ref for repeatable camera restore on renderer replacement.
Existing pointer takeover and native CameraController already supply exact active trajectory revision, seeded star and retention point.
Use true move/down/up events and Three projection of the rendered galaxy, not semantic flags alone.

search_ladder.conclusion: Use the existing pinned YEIS application and its native orbit behavior; no second renderer.
Reuse current R3F render frame and pointer callback; no new state machine, JS event or frame loop.
Apply the existing native OrbitPoint authority at pointer takeover. Keep true camera free flight and endpoints.
Reuse actual in-progress autopilot anchor and existing revision rather than inventing screen picking or restarting flight.

candidates.name: Reuse pinned YEIS gotoPoint anchor and orbitPoint
candidates.source: Exact main and loaded native CameraController
candidates.reason: Same actively painted subject and same physical pose applied in the same render frame; no second input owner.

candidates.name: Install separate Drei camera-controls on the already native Galaxy
candidates.reason: Would create competing input and position owners and lose native floating-frame semantics.

decision.rationale: A scoped subject-preserving pointer takeover is the already established native orbit semantics, not a separate motion engine.
decision.fallback: Do not publish if the unchanged positive-motion direct geometry or cold reset/other owner controls regress.
